metadata.title: IEA International Computer and Information Literacy Study 2018 Assessment Framework

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an assessment framework for ICILS 2018 rather than an empirical analysis paper. It describes the constructs, instruments, and contextual framework used to generate ICILS achievement and questionnaire measures, but it does not report an analytic sample or a statistical estimation procedure with explicit survey-weight variables. As a result, the framework does not specify whether analysts should apply student/sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in model estimation. For downstream empirical ICILS analyses using the released microdata, analysts should follow IEA’s standard complex-sample guidance for ICILS (including the use of provided sampling/replicate weights) to obtain population-representative inferences and correct standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework/assessment-design publication that documents the ICILS 2018 constructs and instrument design, not an empirical study predicting an outcome from ICILS microdata. Because no dependent variable is modeled with PV-based achievement scores and no estimation model is reported, plausible-value handling is not applicable in the sense of PV computation/combining rules. Missing-data handling is also not reported because the document does not run an analysis pipeline on an analytic sample; it focuses on how the assessment is built and administered.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the full available sample for the specified countries is not applicable here because this is not an empirical microdata analysis; it is an ICILS 2018 assessment framework describing constructs, instruments, and contextual variables.

data.outcome_summary: This publication provides the ICILS 2018 assessment framework, explaining the background, constructs, and design of the computer and information literacy (CIL) assessment and the optional computational thinking (CT) domain. It defines the CIL and CT constructs, specifies strands and aspects, and describes how test items and student/context instruments are mapped to the framework. The document also outlines the contextual framework used to classify contextual factors and variables at multiple levels (e.g., student, classroom/school, and system). As a framework, it does not report an empirical analytic sample, model estimation, or performance metrics; instead, it serves as the blueprint for how ICILS measures are operationalized and how participating systems can interpret results. Consequently, there are no ML-based predictive outcomes or PV/missing-data handling results to summarize here.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is an assessment framework rather than an empirical study. It does not contain an ML modeling section, reported target variables, performance metrics, or an analytic sample with country-level Ns, so fields such as total_students, countries, plausible-value handling details, missing-data handling, and main_findings cannot be populated from the provided text. The appropriate interpretation is that the document is methodological and instrument-design oriented, documenting how ICILS 2018 is constructed for later empirical analyses.
